findings.description: A scope-in glob of exactly `./` is now offered as a file to create. Normalizing `./` gives the empty string. globToRegExpSource also turns `./` into `^$`, so the glob matches no tracked path. The empty probe matches `^$`, no protected glob (`.claude/**`, `.pupitre/**`) or plausible scope-out matches `""`, and scopedPaths keeps it. The kickoff then prints "`./`: to be created, no tracked file matches it yet". Before this commit the probe was `./`, which fails `^$`, so nothing was listed. assertPlannableSpec only rejects an all-blank scope-in, so `pup new --scope ./` gets through. A user could easily type `./` meaning the whole repo. The scope is already useless in that case, since it lets the session edit nothing, but the new line points the session at a bogus file to create instead of leaving the kickoff silent.

Duplicated Code. `glob.trim().replace(/^\.\//, '')` is now the third copy of the glob normalization. The others are in `src/core/glob.utils.ts:15` and `src/core/routing.utils.ts:60`. The comment on lines 80-81 says the text is "normalized as globToRegExp reads it", so the correctness of `toCreate` now depends on this copy staying in step with `glob.utils.ts`. If `globToRegExpSource` changes how it normalizes, `toCreate` would silently disagree with the gate. The project rule "no abstraction until third use" is met by this third use. It is still a nit because the copy is one short expression and the behavior is correct today.
